title: Weekly Reset
concept: About 40 minutes, five short parts: thank each other, check the load is fair, take one friction point before it grows, then one ask each and one next step. 15 minutes is fine to start. Tight on time? A 15-minute version still counts, or split it into two shorter sittings in the week. Maintenance, not a trial.
whenToUse: Same day and time each week; also after travel or a hard stretch. Not for a fight: flooded? Pause + Return first.
steps: Appreciation (5 min): each of you names one specific thing.
Check the load (15 min): each of you says whether you’ve felt supported or alone, and whether the load feels fair.
One friction point (15 min): each of you brings one small thing. Agree a next step, not the whole fix.
Requests: each of you makes one specific ask for next week.
Next steps: agree one thing to try and when you’ll check back. Requests and next steps share the last 5 minutes.
Monthly part, once a month, adds 10 minutes: who carried what, any open Proof items, and one ritual to keep, tweak or drop.

phrases.text: I felt supported when ___. I felt alone when ___.

working: A sets forty minutes on the timer and B starts with an appreciation. It ends with the Thursday school run swapped and a check back on Sunday. Neither is saving anything up for a row.
notWorking: B opens with “Can we start with Wednesday?” They skip the appreciation and set no timer. The check-in turns into round two.
activity: Book the next three weeks. Set a 40-minute timer; stop when it rings. Anything bigger waits. Use the Weekly Reset agenda sheet, or the button below.
note: Yearly part, 1 to 2 hours once a year, phones away and nothing booked after. Are you still heading the same way? What do you want to protect, drop or newly agree this year? What does each of you need more of in the next twelve months? If your directions no longer fit, say so. Deciding to part is an honest outcome, not a failure.
